mainTopic: Whether a gift to an unborn baby (עובר) works: רב הונא's rule, רב נחמן's challenge from our משנה, and the failed attempts to find an author for that משנה
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a man who promises a מנה to whoever tells him whether his wife had a boy or a girl. It asks why the messenger is paid when twins are born, answers that the man also mentioned twins, and explains that his conditions leave out only a נפל. Next comes a real case: a man gave his property to the baby his wife was carrying. רב הונא rules that a gift to an עובר does not take effect. רב נחמן challenges him from our משנה, where an unborn boy does receive a מנה, and רב הונא answers that he does not know who taught that משנה. The גמרא then asks why רב הונא did not name an author for the משנה, and suggests רבי מאיר, רבי יוסי, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and a combination of the last two. Each suggestion is rejected, because none of these תנאים clearly allows a gift to a receiver who is not yet born. Finally, the גמרא tries to read the משנה as being about a reward for a messenger, or about a baby who was already born. Both readings are rejected from the wording at the end of the משנה.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the man who rewards the one who brings him news of the birth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a man promises a מנה to whoever tells him the baby is a boy, and a מנה if it is a girl. If twins are born, a boy and a girl, the messenger still gets only one מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A man said, 'Whoever tells me what my wife gave birth to: if it is a boy, he gets a מנה.' If she had a boy, the messenger gets a מנה. He also said, 'If it is a girl, a מנה.' If she had a girl, the messenger gets a מנה. If she had a boy and a girl, the messenger gets only one מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the discussion it was in the middle of. The ברייתא is about a reward for a messenger who reports the birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man set up separate conditions for a boy and for a girl, with the same reward for each. The ברייתא says that if twins come, the messenger does not collect twice. He gets only one מנה. The next steps explain why he gets anything at all for twins.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth one hundred זוז

steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא the money goes to the messenger who brings the news, not to the baby. Keep this separate from the later case, where the money goes to the child.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'Whoever informs me with what'
my wife's womb has opened;
phrases.notes: A polite way of asking whether the baby is a boy or a girl.

phrases.english: if it is a male, he shall take a maneh,'
if she gave birth to a male, he takes a maneh.
'If it is a female, a maneh';
if she gave birth to a female, he takes a maneh;
if she gave birth to a male and a female,
he has only a maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the discussion that came just before this section of the daf.
steps.raayaObject: How a reward promised for a birth works when twins are born

steps.title: The man never mentioned twins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the messenger gets anything for twins, since the man only spoke about a boy or a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he never said anything about 'a boy and a girl'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the end of the ברייתא. The man's conditions covered only a boy or only a girl, so why is the messenger paid when twins are born?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Conditions are read as they were said. Twins are a different situation from 'a boy' or 'a girl', so maybe no condition was met at all and the messenger should get nothing.

phrases.english: But 'a male and a female' he did not say!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling at the end of the ברייתא about twins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the messenger gets a מנה when twins are born
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man's stated conditions did not include twins, so it seems no condition was fulfilled.

steps.title: He also mentioned twins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where the man also said that twins would earn a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he also said, 'If it is a boy and a girl, he also gets a מנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the man did include twins in his offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shortened what the man said. He actually had a third condition for twins, so paying one מנה follows exactly what he said.

phrases.english: Where he also said: 'If a male and a female,'
he shall also take a maneh.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about twins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the man said more than the ברייתא quotes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man only spoke about a single boy or a single girl.
steps.terutzMaskana: He also made a condition for twins, so the messenger gets a מנה.

steps.title: Then what is left out?
steps.stepSummary: If the man listed boy, girl, and twins, what birth is not included in his conditions?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what was he trying to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the man seems to have covered every possible birth, so the גמרא asks what all these conditions exclude. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every birth earns a מנה, he could simply have said 'whoever tells me she gave birth.' Spelling out each option suggests that some outcome is not covered.

phrases.english: But to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer that the man covered all three options.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which birth outcome is not covered by the man's conditions

steps.title: A baby that is not viable is left out
steps.stepSummary: The conditions exclude a נפל, a baby that will not survive. For that news the messenger gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude a נפל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the man was leaving out a נפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'boy', 'girl', and 'twins', the man meant living, healthy babies. News of a נפל is not good news, so no reward is owed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born not able to survive

steps.whatToRemember: The messenger gets one מנה for a boy, a girl, or twins, because the man stated all three. He gets nothing for a נפל.

phrases.english: To exclude a non-viable newborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the conditions exclude.

steps.title: A gift to an unborn baby does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: A man gave his property to the baby his wife was carrying. רב הונא rules that this is a gift to an עובר, and an עובר cannot acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man said to his wife: 'My property is for the baby you are carrying.' רב הונא said: This is giving ownership to an עובר, and when someone gives ownership to an עובר, the עובר does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a real case, and רב הונא gives his ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man tried to give his property to a baby that was not yet born. רב הונא holds that a baby still in the womb cannot become an owner, so the gift does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives ownership to an unborn baby

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic rule: an עובר cannot receive a gift. The rest of the discussion tests that rule.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his wife:
My property is for this one with whom you are pregnant.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הָוֵי מְזַכֶּה לְעוּבָּר,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: This is one who transfers ownership to a fetus,
and one who transfers ownership to a fetus, it does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: gifts to an unborn baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מְזַכֶּה לְעוּבָּר לֹא קָנָה: an unborn baby cannot acquire a gift.

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says that if a man promised a מנה when his wife has a boy, and she has a boy, the child takes it. That looks like a gift to an עובר that works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged רב הונא: If someone says, 'If my wife has a boy, he gets a מנה,' and she has a boy, the boy takes the מנה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב הונא's rule using our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the father gives money to a baby who is not born yet, and the baby receives it. That seems to show an עובר can acquire, against רב הונא.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the messenger ברייתא from the start. In our משנה the money goes to the baby himself.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman raised an objection to Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹמֵר ״אִם יָלְדָה אִשְׁתִּי זָכָר – יִטּוֹל מָנֶה״,
phrases.english: One who says: 'If my wife gives birth to a male, he shall take a maneh,'
if she gave birth to a male, he takes a maneh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that מְזַכֶּה לְעוּבָּר לֹא קָנָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה lets an unborn boy receive the מנה his father promised him, so an עובר can acquire.

steps.title: רב הונא: I do not know whose view our משנה follows
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא does not explain the משנה. He says he does not know who taught it, so he does not have to follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our משנה, I do not know who taught it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge by setting the משנה aside, not by explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא does not claim the משנה agrees with him. He says it does not match any known opinion, so he keeps his rule that an עובר cannot acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know who taught it

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא holds that a gift to an עובר does not work. He deals with our משנה by saying he does not know whose opinion it follows.

phrases.english: He said to him: Our mishna,
I do not know who taught it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ – אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי שְׁנָאָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב הונא's answer to רב נחמן's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting aside the source as following no known opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה shows that an עובר can acquire.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is of unknown authorship, so רב הונא's rule stands.

steps.title: Why not say the משנה follows רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב הונא did not answer that our משנה follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him answer: the משנה follows רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב הונא's answer. Instead of saying 'I don't know who taught it,' he could have named a תנא, רבי מאיר, who might agree with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says you can transfer something that does not exist yet, like fruit that has not grown. The suggestion is that if he allows that, he might also allow giving to a baby that has not been born. Then the משנה would have a known author, and רב הונא would simply be ruling against רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him (why didn't he answer this way?)
Something that has not yet come into the world

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
phrases.notes: רב הונא could have given this answer to רב נחמן, who challenged him from our משנה.

phrases.english: It is רבי מאיר's view,
who says: a person can transfer ownership of
something that has not yet come into the world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer from step 8 by offering a known author for the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that he does not know who taught the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There seems to be a known תנא, רבי מאיר, whose view could explain the משנה, so רב הונא could have named him.

steps.title: רבי מאיר only spoke about giving to someone who exists
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: רבי מאיר allows transferring a not-yet-existing item to an existing person, but we never heard him allow giving to someone who does not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard רבי מאיר say this about giving to someone who is already in the world. About giving to someone who is not yet in the world, did you hear him say it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: רבי מאיר's rule does not fit our case. So רב הונא could not use him to explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different problems: the item does not exist yet, or the receiver does not exist yet. רבי מאיר only solved the first one. An unborn baby is the second problem, a receiver who is not yet in the world, and רבי מאיר never addressed that.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone or something that already exists
Did you hear him say this? (No, you did not)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the item and the receiver. רבי מאיר lets the ITEM be not yet in the world. Here the RECEIVER, the baby, is the one not yet in the world.

phrases.english: Say that you heard רבי מאיר say this
about giving to someone who is in the world;
about giving to someone who is not yet in the world,
did you hear him say it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבי מאיר suggestion from step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבי מאיר as the author of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר's rule is about an item that does not exist yet, not about a receiver who does not exist yet.

steps.title: Why not say the משנה follows רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another known author: רבי יוסי, who holds that an unborn baby can own things, as shown by a משנה about slaves and תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him answer: the משנה follows רבי יוסי, who says an unborn baby acquires! As we learned: an unborn baby disqualifies and does not let others eat, these are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to find an author for our משנה, this time רבי יוסי. It brings a משנה showing that רבי יוסי treats an unborn baby as an owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the quoted משנה, a כהן died and left his wife pregnant. The unborn baby's share in the father's slaves stops them from eating תרומה. That only makes sense if the baby already owns part of them, so רבי יוסי seems to hold that an unborn baby can own property.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion given to a כהן, eaten only by a כהן's household

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
It is רבי יוסי's view,
who says: an unborn baby acquires!
As we learned: an unborn baby disqualifies
phrases.notes: This is from יבמות 67a: a כהן died leaving his wife pregnant, and the baby's share in his slaves stops them from eating תרומה.

phrases.english: and does not let others eat; these are the words of רבי יוסי.
phrases.notes: The unborn baby does not let its mother eat תרומה, even though its father was a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא, דְּאָמַר: עוּבָּר קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי מאיר was rejected, offers a second known author for the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that he does not know who taught the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי holds that an unborn baby can own property, so the משנה could follow him and רב הונא could have named him.

steps.title: Inheritance is different from a gift
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: רבי יוסי only spoke about ירושה, which comes on its own, not about a מתנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Inheritance is different, because it comes by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the רבי יוסי suggestion. His case was about inheriting, which is not the same as receiving a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ירושה passes to the heir automatically, with no act of acquiring needed. A מתנה needs a real act of acquiring, and an unborn baby cannot do that. So רבי יוסי's view does not explain our משנה, and רב הונא's 'I don't know who taught it' stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift, which needs a real act of acquiring

steps.whatToRemember: Neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יוסי allows giving a gift to an unborn baby. רבי מאיר spoke about items not yet in existence, and רבי יוסי spoke about ירושה, which comes on its own. So רב הונא could not name an author for the משנה, and his ruling stands: an עובר cannot receive a gift.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key line: an unborn baby can receive a ירושה but not a מתנה, because a gift needs an act of acquiring.

phrases.english: Inheritance is different,
since it comes by itself.
phrases.notes: Nobody has to do anything for an inheritance to pass. A gift needs an act of acquiring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבי יוסי suggestion from step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבי יוסי as the author of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's ruling is about ירושה, which needs no act of acquiring. It does not show that an unborn baby can receive a מתנה.

steps.title: Why not say the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רב הונא could have said the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who treats a gift to an heir the same as an inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רב הונא answer that the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who holds that inheritance and gift are the same. As we learned: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says that if a person said his property goes to someone who is fit to inherit him, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers רב הונא a new way out. Maybe the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי (Step 11) only allowed an unborn baby to get a ירושה, not a מתנה. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says a gift to a fitting heir works just like a ירושה. So maybe his view closes that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to inherit him, meaning one of his legal heirs
His words stand, so his statement takes effect

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא,
phrases.english: But let him say to him: It is the view of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה,

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַר: לָא שְׁנָא יְרוּשָּׁה וְלָא שְׁנָא מַתָּנָה!
phrases.english: who says: inheritance is no different and a gift is no different!

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר עַל מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ –
phrases.english: If he said about someone who is fit to inherit him,
his words stand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוסי was rejected because he only spoke about ירושה, this step brings a תנא who treats a gift like a ירושה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that he does not know who taught the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a known תנא, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, whose rule could explain the משנה, so רב הונא should have used it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה spoke only about someone already born
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה only spoke about giving to someone who already exists, not to someone not yet born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה say this about someone who exists in the world. Did he say it about someone who is not yet in the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from Step 13. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה never talked about an unborn receiver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule only says a gift to an heir works like an inheritance. The heir in his case is already alive. Our משנה needs a gift to a baby not yet born, and he never said that works.

keyTerms.meaning: Something or someone that exists in the world now
Something or someone not yet in the world

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה –
phrases.english: Say that you heard רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה say this
about someone who is in the world;
about someone who is not in the world, did he say it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the use of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה alone as the author of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His rule was only said about a receiver who already exists, not an unborn one.

steps.title: Combine רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and that he also agrees with רבי יוסי that an unborn baby can own things.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רב הונא answer that the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and that he holds like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to join the two earlier ideas together into one answer for רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says an unborn baby can get a ירושה (Step 11). רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says a gift works like a ירושה (Step 13). Put together, an unborn baby could get a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like, meaning he agrees with

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא,
phrases.english: But let him say to him: It is the view of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה,
and he holds like רבי יוסי!
phrases.notes: He agrees that an unborn baby can inherit, as we saw in Step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא, וְסָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the weakness found in Steps 12 and 14 by combining both תנאים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that he does not know who taught the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Joining the two views covers both needs, an unborn receiver and a gift, so רב הונא could have answered this way.

steps.title: No proof he agrees with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: who says רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה agrees with רבי יוסי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Who says that he holds like him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the combined answer from Step 15 in one short line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot build an author for the משנה out of two separate opinions. There is no source showing that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה accepts רבי יוסי's rule about unborn babies.

keyTerms.meaning: Who says? We have no proof

phrases.english: Who says that he holds like him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The combined author made of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי יוסי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Nothing shows that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה agrees with רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about a reward for good news
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה is not about a gift to the baby at all. It is about a reward to whoever brings the news of the birth, and that person is already alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רב הונא answer that the משנה is about someone who said: "whoever brings me the good news" gets the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops looking for an author and tries a new reading of the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money goes to the messenger who reports the birth, the receiver already exists. Then there is no problem of giving to someone not yet born.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever brings me the good news

phrases.english: But let him say to him: it is about "whoever informs me"!
phrases.notes: The father said, "whoever tells me my wife had a boy gets this money."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the search for an author fails, the גמרא suggests a different case for the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that he does not know who taught the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the receiver is the messenger, who is alive now, the משנה fits רב הונא's view with no need for a special author.

steps.title: The end of the משנה talks about an heir
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: the end of the משנה says that if he is the only heir, he inherits everything. That makes no sense if the case is about a messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at what the end of the משנה teaches: "If there is no heir besides him, he inherits everything." If the case is about "whoever informs me," what is an heir doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from Step 17 by pointing to the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה talks about the baby as an heir. That shows the משנה is about the baby himself, not a messenger. So the "good news" reading does not fit, and רב נחמן's challenge against רב הונא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the משנה
What is it doing here? Why is it mentioned?

steps.whatToRemember: So far, every attempt to explain the משנה for רב הונא has failed, and one more attempt follows in Step 19. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה only spoke about people already alive. We cannot assume he agrees with רבי יוסי. The "good news" reading clashes with the end of the משנה. That is why רב הונא simply said he does not know who taught it.

phrases.english: If so, regarding what the end of the משנה teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם יוֹרֵשׁ אֶלָּא הוּא – יוֹרֵשׁ הַכֹּל;
phrases.english: "And if there is no heir there except him, he inherits everything";
if it is about "whoever informs me," what is an heir doing here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the משנה is about a reward to the messenger
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The end of the משנה talks about an heir, which does not fit a case about a messenger.

steps.title: Maybe the baby was already born
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב הונא could answer that the משנה is talking about a gift made after the wife had already given birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רב הונא answer רב נחמן: the משנה is about a case where she already gave birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way for רב הונא to answer רב נחמן: the משנה is about a baby who was already born, so it is not a gift to an unborn baby at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's problem was that a gift cannot be given to someone who does not exist yet. If the baby was already born when the father spoke, and he simply did not know yet whether it was a boy or girl, the baby already exists. Then the משנה does not contradict רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him: a suggested answer

phrases.english: But let him say to him: it is where she already gave birth!
phrases.notes: He means רב הונא should answer רב נחמן this way. The baby was born, but the father did not yet know if it was a boy or a girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the messenger explanation fails in step 18, the גמרא tries a different way to set up the משנה's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the baby already exists at the time of the gift.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to describe a gift to a baby not yet born, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the birth already happened, the recipient exists, and רב הונא's rule stands.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that he does not know who taught the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the gift was made after the birth, the receiver already exists, so the משנה fits רב הונא's rule and he did not need to set it aside.

steps.title: The משנה's future wording rules this out
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected, because the end of the משנה says 'whatever my wife will give birth to,' which is future language.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at what the end of the משנה teaches: if he said 'whatever my wife will give birth to shall take,' that baby takes. Why does it say 'will give birth'? It should have said 'gave birth'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 19 by pointing to the exact wording of the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה quotes the father saying 'כל מה שתלד אשתי,' meaning 'whatever my wife WILL give birth to.' That clearly speaks about a birth that has not happened yet. If the baby were already born, the משנה would have written 'כל שילדה,' 'whatever she gave birth to.'

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the משנה
That she will give birth to (future tense)
That she gave birth to (past tense)

steps.confusionAlert: The whole proof is about tense: 'תלד' (will give birth) versus 'ילדה' (gave birth). The question is not what kind of baby was born, but whether the birth had happened yet.

phrases.english: If so, regarding what the end of the משנה teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר ״כׇּל מַה שֶּׁתֵּלֵד אִשְׁתִּי – יִטּוֹל״,
phrases.english: And if he said, 'Whatever my wife will give birth to shall take,'
then this one takes;
phrases.notes: In the משנה, the baby born here is a טומטום, and even so it receives the gift.

phrases.english: 'Whatever she will give birth to'?!
It should have said, 'Whatever she gave birth to'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 19 using the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that the משנה is about a baby already born.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה uses future tense ('שתלד'), which only fits a baby not yet born.
steps.whatToRemember: Every attempt to explain the משנה for רב הונא failed. רבי מאיר and רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה only spoke about receivers already alive. רבי יוסי spoke only about ירושה. We cannot assume רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה agrees with רבי יוסי. The "good news" reading clashes with the mention of an heir, and the "already born" reading clashes with the future tense שֶּׁתֵּלֵד. That is why רב הונא simply said he does not know who taught the משנה.
